content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper upgrades AWP (weight perturbation on all adversarial examples) to RWP (weight perturbation on adversarial examples with small classification loss) to enhance adversarial training, which helps to improve robustness.
content.main_review:
Main Concerns:

**Page 5, 6:**  
**Authors: LSC View of Robust Overfitting: the model will first memorize some easy-to-learn adversarial examples, and then spread to the entire training dataset...**

This conclusion is only supported by one experiment in Figure 2. Is this phenomenon general across datasets, networks, and attack methods? Can you provide more empirical results? Can you provide an insightful (theoretical) analysis to answer why the model will first memorize some easy-to-learn adversarial examples...?  


**Authors: LSC view of Adversarial Weight Perturbation: adversarial weight perturbation on adversarial examples with small classification loss is sufficient to suppress robust overfitting, adversarial weight perturbation on adversarial examples with large classification loss leads to worse adversarial robustness.**

This paper also argues the above conclusion through one experiment in Figure 1c. Is this general? What are the real reasons behind it? 
In Figure 1c, what's the percentage for each LSC group? Does the percentage affect results? 


**Authors: Do We Really Need the Worst-case Weight Perturbation?: conducting worst-case weight perturbation on these adversarial examples is not necessary, since it will also deteriorate the adversarial robustness.**

Why it will deteriorate the adversarial robustness, can you provide more theoretical and empirical analyses? Compared with AT, I don't see 'deteriorate' in Figure 1c.


Minor concerns.

**Page 4:** 
Although AWP is not proposed by this work, the explanation for 'Does Weight Perturbation Robustness Lead to Better Adversarial Robustness?' through one experiment (Figure1(a)) is weak. Is the experiment in Figure1(a) general across datasets, attack methods, networks? Or can you provide some theoretical analysis?

As the article structure and empirical settings are (very) similar with AWP https://arxiv.org/pdf/2004.05884.pdf, why don't compare with MART in Table 2 (which is shown in AWP Table 2)?

The improvements in Table2 under auto-attack are narrow  (for me, auto-attack is an important target)
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper provides a minor upgrade for AWP to enhance adversarial training, but it is short of enough contribution (ref Main Concerns).  e.g., no clear and enough (empirical and theoretical) explanations for  'LSC View of Robust Overfitting, LSC view of Adversarial Weight Perturbation, Do We Really Need the Worst-case Weight Perturbation?'.

In conclusion, 1. the current version is a small modification of AWP (RWP is AWP with loss threshold), 2. and just uses a small number of experiments in Figure 1, 2 to explain the motivation of RWP. Lack of theoretical analysis or insightful view. 3. Some experiment results are narrow (e.g., auto attacks in Table 2). For these reasons, I think this paper has a lot of room for improvement.

content.comment:
We sincerely thank you for your comprehensive comments on our paper and please find our answers to your questions below.

**Q1**:"This conclusion is only supported by one experiment in Figure 2. Is this phenomenon...."

**A1**:1)Yes, this phenomenon is general across datasets, networks and attack modes. we verify the phenomenon by removing the training examples. Specifically, during the adversarial training process, we remove training examples whose loss value is lower than the LSC value. In this way, we demonstrate the generalities of the phenomenon under different attack modes, different datasets and different models, as shown in the Appendix of revision. 2)The memorization effects [a] of deep networks show that they will first memorize simple patterns (e.g., easy data) and then abnormal or noisy data. In the adversarial training process, there are some examples that are still easy to learn after adversarial attacks (e.g., adversarial examples with small loss). In the process of fitting these adversarial examples, the network will also fit the generated adversarial noise, which eventually leads to robust overfitting. Therefore, the key to eliminating robust overfitting is to prevent the network from fitting these easy adversarial examples. For this purpose, we designed the proposed algorithm.

[a]Devansh Arpit et al. A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks. ICML 2017

**Q2**:"This paper also argues the above conclusion through one experiment in Figure 1c...."

**A2**:1)Yes, this is general across datasets, networks and attack modes, which can be verified by the performance improvement in Table 1. 2) The real reason we suppose is that weight perturbation hinders network optimization. If there is no robust overfitting in adversarial training, then the standard training should be able to achieve better adversarial robustness. Adversarial weight perturbation can suppress robust overfitting, which brings a certain degree of robustness improvement, but weight perturbation itself hinders network optimization. 3) The percentage of training examples below the LSC value is about 40% before 100 epoch, about 65% for 100 to 150 epoch, and about 90% for 150 to 200 epoch. The percentage is mainly related to the LSC value, which will affect the experimental results.

**Q3**:"Why it will deteriorate the adversarial robustness, can you provide more...."

**A3**:The degradation here refers to the comparison with the RWP algorithm, not the comparison with AT. The robustness achieved by this method and RWP are 57.4 and 58.55, respectively.

**Q4**:"Although AWP is not proposed by this work, the explanation for 'Does Weight Perturbation Robustness Lead to Better Adversarial Robustness?' through...."

**A4**:Yes, the experiment in Figure 1(a) is general across datasets, attack modes and networks. Similar patten has been observed on different datasets (CIFAR10, SVHN, and CIFAR100), attack modes (Linf and L2) and networks (PreAct ResNet18 and Wide ResNet32-10).

**Q5**:"As the article structure and empirical settings are (very) similar with AWP...."

**A5**:Because our computing resources are very limited, the adversarial training on wide ResNet in Table 2 generally takes more than 7 days. content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors aim to achieve a balance of decreasing robust over-fitting and adversarial robustness. They propose a criterion, termed loss stationary condition (LSC), by dividing the adversarial examples into different groups based on their classification loss. With such partition, they find that the network would first overfit these adversarial examples with small classification loss. Following these empirical observations, they further propose to only perform the weight perturbation strategy on examples with a smaller loss. Experimental results show that such a strategy can improve adversarial robustness.
content.main_review:
[Strengths]
1. This paper is clearly written and very easy to follow.
2. This paper has a good motivation for the research problem (i.e., how to address the conflict between the current weight perturbation methods and the adversarial robustness).
3. This paper shows an interesting observation: the adversarial examples group with small classification error has a significantly larger generalization gap. Based on the above observations, this paper proposes a new robust weight perturbation strategy, which can improve the adversarial robustness.


[Weaknesses]
1. The contribution is incremental. Based on some new empirical observations, this paper proposes a trick to improve the AWP method. The novelty is limited, and the contribution is incremental.

2. The goal of this paper is not clear. Compared to the original weight perturbation method AWP, is the essence of this paper to further decrease the robust over-fitting or improve robustness? The two issues both will lead to the improvement of testing robustness, how to distinguish them in this paper? This paper only compares the testing robustness between the proposed method and AWP, but does not clarify their differences in the generalization gap.

3. The proposed method is not well-motivated, i.e., the authors don’t introduce the motivation of the LSC criterion. Why do the authors analyze the generalization gap from such a LSC perspective? Such flaw makes the work seem to be built upon an accidental discovery from empirical observations.

4. There lacks a thorough explanation of the rationale behind the proposed method. This paper is mainly built upon the empirical observations in Figures 1 and 2. However, why such examples will result in a larger generalization gap? A theoretical analysis (even informal) is expected. Instead, the author only mentioned that “the model will first memorize some easy-to-learn adversarial examples, and then spread to the entire training dataset”.

5. The empirical observations lack enough evidence. The phenomena in section 3, including “weight perturbation robustness and adversarial robustness are not actually mutually beneficial” and “The DNN first overfit adversarial samples with small classification error”, are just verified on a few architectures and datasets. Hence, it cannot be guaranteed that such phenomena are accidental or regular. The authors are suggested to perform abundant experiments with different DNNs on different datasets to verify the ubiquity of such phenomena.

6. Experimental results are not convincing enough to support the claim of this paper : the proposed method “prevents deep networks from over-fitting while avoiding the side effect of excessive weight perturbation, significantly improving the robustness of adversarial training.”
(1) The authors have not conducted experiments to indicate that the proposed method can reduce the robustness over-fitting. 
(2) Results reported in Table 1 only shows a marginal improvement, compared to other baseline methods.


7. The setting of the hyper-parameter is questionable. This paper used two parameters 1.7 and 2.2, which is not usual in the grid search setting. Why not use sequences like [0,0.5,1,1.5,2]? Such a parameter setting would be deemed to be cherry-picked, such that the effectiveness and generalization capacity of the proposed method would be doubted.

8. The term “loss stationary criterion” sounds inconsistent with the paper. Actually, the LSC is a simple operation to divide the adversarial examples into different groups based on their classification loss. I can’t get why to use the word “stationary” and “criterion”. How to understand “stationary” and “criterion” here?


[Minors]
1. The legend in the figures are too small to read.
content.summary_of_the_review: The main problems of this paper lie on the following two aspects: (i) The proposed method is not well-motivated, i.e., it is unclear why the authors chose LSC to divide the adversarial samples into several groups. Such flaw makes the work seem to be built upon an accidental discovery from empirical observations. (ii) This paper proposes a trick to improve the AWP method, so the contribution is incremental. In addition, this paper lacks a thorough explanation of the rationale behind the proposed method. Therefore, I suggest a rejection decision.

content.title: Author Reply to Reviewer 8qVH (Part 1)
content.comment:
We sincerely thank you for your comprehensive comments on our paper and please find our answers to your questions below.

**Q1**:"The contribution is incremental. Based on some new empirical...."

**A1**:We found that the model first overfits some easy-to-learn adversarial examples, and then expands to the entire dataset. Although this is an empirical discovery, this phenomenon is generalized in different attack modes, different datasets and different network structures. We believe that this phenomenon is meaningful for in-depth understanding and analysis of robust overfitting, and it provides a new perspective for eliminating robust overfitting in adversarial training. Based on this phenomenon, we further optimized the weight perturbation strategy and can achieve better adversarial robustness. We agree that the proposed weight perturbation method itself is incremental, but the purpose of this is to verify the effectiveness of the aforementioned phenomenon. In summary, we may disagree that the contribution of this paper is incremental.

**Q2**:"The goal of this paper is not clear. Compared to the original weight perturbation...."

**A2**:The goal of our paper is to eliminate robust overfitting, which also leads to robust performance improvements and reduces the generalization gap. The generalization gap of RWP is larger than that of AWP. It is because that our algorithm does not take the reduction of generalization gap as the optimization goal like AWP. We observed an interesting and general phenomenon in robust overfitting, and then validated our ideas using the weight perturbation method. The performance comparison with AWP is to demonstrate the effectiveness of our ideas.

**Q3**:"The proposed method is not well-motivated, i.e., the authors don’t introduce the motivation of the LSC criterion...."

**A3**:We observed an interesting and general phenomenon: the model first overfits adversarial examples that are easy to learn, and then expands to the entire dataset. The LSC criterion is used to help us analyze experimental phenomena and guide algorithm design.

**Q4**:"There lacks a thorough explanation of the rationale behind the proposed method. This paper...."

**A4**:The memorization effects [a] of deep networks show that they will first memorize simple patterns (e.g., easy data) and then abnormal or noisy data. In the adversarial training process, there are some examples that are still easy to learn after adversarial attacks (e.g., adversarial examples with small loss). In the process of memorization of these adversarial examples, the network will also fit the generated adversarial noise, which eventually leads to robust overfitting. Therefore, the key to eliminating robust overfitting is to prevent the network from fitting these easy adversarial examples. For this purpose, we designed the proposed algorithm.

[a]Devansh Arpit et al. A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks. ICML 2017

**Q5**:"The empirical observations lack enough evidence. The phenomena in...."

**A5**:We verify the phenomenon (the model first overfits some easy-to-learn examples, and then expands to the entire dataset) by removing the training examples. Specifically, during the adversarial training process, we remove training examples whose loss value is lower than the LSC value. In this way, we demonstrate the generalities of the phenomenon under different attack modes, different datasets and different models, as shown in the Appendix of revision. The generalization of the phenomenon that weight perturbation hinders network optimization can be verified by the experimental results of table 1.

**Q6**:"Experimental results are not convincing enough to support the claim of this paper...."

**A6**: (1) Figure 3(c) clearly shows that our proposed method is able to prevent deep networks from robust overfitting. (2) The performance comparison with AWP is to verify the observed overfitting phenomenon. Besides, AWP is a strong state-of-the-art baseline. On this basis, our proposed method can achieve a stable performance improvement, fully verifying the effectiveness of our method.

**Q7**:"The setting of the hyper-parameter is questionable. This paper...."

**A7**: The LSC value is a key hyper-parameter in our algorithm, and the detailed tuning is to fully prove the effectiveness of our method. We observed that the LSC value is not sensitive to different network structure. It is sensitive to the classes of the dataset, such as CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. In practice, we can estimate the LSC value according to the number of categories of the dataset. For example, 1.5 can achieve good results for both CIFAR-10 and SVHN, and 4 for CIFAR-100.

display_title: Official Review of Paper1055 by Reviewer PMmu

content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose a variant of adversarial weight perturbations to improve adversarial robustness obtained through adversarial training. Specifically, they compute the adversarial weight perturbations only based on adversarial examples not exceeding a particular loss threshold.
content.main_review:
Strengths:
- The paper is clearly structured, related work is discussed sufficiently and experimental setup is provided in detail.
- Addressing the question which adversarial examples to compute the weight perturbation on is interesting as adversarial training is known to overfit badly, especially on non-robust examples where large loss values are observed.
- Experiments with vanilla AT, TRADES and RST, evaluation using the standard AA benchmark.
- Ablation studies with respect to key parameters.
- Adversarial robustness is shown to improve over baselines.

Weaknesses:
- Writing can be improved at times. For example, in the abstract it is not clear how weight perturbations undermine robustness or what is meant with “excessive weight perturbation”. Similar sentences are found throughout the paper. A more specific language would be useful.
- Also, regarding the last paragraph in the introduction, the AT-AWP paper actually provides some experiments highlighting the extent to which weight perturbations are useful (how many iterations, comparing to random weight perturbations etc.).
- In Figure 1: what is gamma? Is it chosen as in the AT-AWP paper?
- A recent ICCV paper [a] also shows that the performance gain of AT-AWP is mainly due to avoiding robust overfitting. It also includes a training plot with loss on correct and incorrectly classified examples that can be seen as a very coarse set of two LSC groups and it actually measures flatness instead of visualizing loss landscapes.

[a] https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.04448

- Why are the LSC groups in between 0 and 3? [a] shows that loss can be significantly larger, especially on mis-classified examples throughout training.
- Regarding the results in Figure 2, I am not convinced that I see a significant trend as highlighted in the text. The text says that in between epochs 100 and 120 the loss on small loss adversarial examples is “obviously” sharper. But I find that very difficulty to see from plots (f) to (k). In fact, I find the blue curve to be flatter in many cases, at least for smaller neighborhoods around zero. Generally, I find these visualizations not very insightful in supporting the authors point. Maybe the authors could try actually measuring flatness following [a] throughout training for the different LSC groups?
- I am also missing a discussion about not computing the gradient on large loss adversarial examples with weight perturbations but without. Until the end of section 3, it reads as if it might hurt to apply weight perturbations on large loss adversarial examples. But as with AT-AWP, the weight perturbation is applied on the full batch – the difference is just which adversarial examples are used to compute the weight perturbation. Wouldn’t it be meaningful to change that and just apply weight perturbation on low loss adversarial examples, too? Of course it is somewhat unclear how to do this with mini-batch training.
- Is the weight perturbation initialized randomly before the K_2 = 10 steps are run?
- How would the results in Table 1 look with AA? Currently, there are no result son SVHN or CIFAR100 with AA, so it is impossible to compare those with other papers or results. Especially as improvement on SVHN and CIFAR100 are less significant for PGD-20 already, so they might reduce more with AA.
- The improvement is most significant for TRADES, while being less significant for AT or RST. It is also unclear how “lucky” the improvement of 0.31 for RST is? Did the authors run multiple models to get an idea of the standard deviation?
- In the AT-AWP paper, one iteration works best, what is the authors opinion on why K_2=10 suddenly works better with RWP?
- Also, using K_2=10 adds a significant computational overhead, so I am unsure whether the comparison in Table 2 is entirely fair. Did you try other baselines that use double the computation? AT with 20 iterations instead of 10, or AT-AWP with more weight perturbation steps. It is essentially missing in Table 2 that AT-AWP needs one forward/backward passes more than AT, but AT-RWP needs 10 forward/backward passes more than AT. I would expect some more meaningful baselines. I can imagine that the small improvement, e.g., for AT, from 54.04 to 54.61 is partly due to more computation (as this is also a WRN-34-10 with quite a bit of capacity).
- I also assume that Table includes early stopped results, right? This should be made explicit in the text or table.
content.summary_of_the_review: I am not sure whether this paper is ready for ICLR. While the results indicate a slight improvement, the analysis of the proposed method is not convincing to me (mainly due to the visualizations) and experiments could be improved (AA on SVHN, CIFAR100, discussion/fair comparison regarding number of forward/backward passes used). I encourage the authors to address the points raised above in their rebuttal.

**A4**:Thank you for pointing out this recent paper. We will provide discussion on this paper in our revision.

**Q5**:"Why are the LSC groups in between 0 and 3? [a] shows that...."

**A5**: Because we found that the model first overfits some training examples with relatively small loss, the LSC group range of [0,3] is sufficient for our analysis.

**Q6**:"Regarding the results in Figure 2, I am not convinced that...."

**A6**:We agree that the weight loss landscape here is not intuitive enough. Thank you very much. Instead, we verify the phenomenon (the model first overfits some easy-to-learn examples, and then expands to the entire dataset) by removing the training examples. Specifically, during the adversarial training process, we remove training examples whose loss value is lower than the LSC value. In this way, we verify the generalities of the phenomenon under different attack modes, different datasets and different networks, as shown in the Appendix of revision. We suppose that these visualizations can fully support and verify our point.

**Q7**:"I am also missing a discussion about not computing the gradient on large loss adversarial examples...."

**A7**: If there is no robust overfitting in adversarial training, then the standard adversarial training without weight perturbation should be able to achieve better adversarial robustness. Adversarial weight perturbation can suppress robust overfitting, which brings a certain degree of robustness improvement, but weight perturbation itself hinders network optimization to some extent. Our view is that the network first overfits some easy-to-learn examples, and then expands to the entire dataset. The key to eliminating robust overfitting is to prevent the network from overfitting these easy-to-learn examples. Therefore, we think it is meaningful to just apply weight perturbation on low loss adversarial examples. The goal of weight perturbation is to increase the loss of these adversarial examples, so that the network is unable to overfit them.

**Q8**:"Is the weight perturbation initialized randomly before the K_2 = 10 steps are run?"

display_title: Official Review of Paper1055 by Reviewer nnPq

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper investigates the extent of Adversarial Weight Perturbation (AWP) that is helpful to avoid robust overfitting and thereby proposes a criterion to regulate the extent of weight perturbation to improve the potential of adversarial training. Authors categorize the adversarial examples into different groups based on their proposed Loss Stationary Condition (LSC), which simply groups the adversarial examples based on their classification loss values. They show that model tend to overfit to the adversarial examples with lower classification loss. Hence, they propose to introduce weight perturbation only to the adversarial examples with lower classification loss and no weight perturbation for higher classification loss samples. Results show that this criterion allows the adversarial training to improve the robustness on SVHN, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100.
content.main_review:
Strengths:
* Problem motivation is clear
* Well written and structured
* Provide a study with regards to the relation of weight perturbation size to adversarial robustness and shown that both are not mutually beneficial.
* Provide an illustration of weight loss landscape that reveal the adversarial examples with lower classification loss are fit overfitted.
* Propose a simple add-on criterion that enable and disable the weight perturbation based on the classification loss value.
* Propose a new strategy to generate the weight perturbation.
* Improves adversarial robustness on SVHN and CIFAR-10 over the baselines.

Concerns:
* Different groups in LSC for CIFAR-10 are manually created. How to choose the groups for a new dataset or dataset with different number of classes or a new model?

* Improvement of results for CIFAR-100 are marginal over the baseline. Does it require carefully tuned LSC groups? or the rate of overfitting is not as evident as CIFAR-10? How does the weight loss landscape look here?

* The improvements of TRADES-AWP and RST-AWP on CIFAR-10 are also marginal. This reveals that the rate of overfitting is not prominent for these models. How does the weight loss landscapes look for these models?

Minor comments:
Given the statement "Without an appropriate criterion to regulate...... unleash its full power" in the Introduction, a teaser figure or table supporting this statement would have been helpful.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper proposes a simple approach to reduce the robust overfitting and improve adversarial training robustness. However, the results are limited to certain settings e.g. Standard adversarial training with CIFAR-10. Results are marginal for different datasets and more robust models. This raises question on the wide range of applicability of the approach. Hence, I tend to rate below acceptance. However, I am willing to reconsider my rating based on other reviews and author responses.

content.title: Author Reply to Reviewer nnPq
content.comment:
We sincerely thank you for your comprehensive comments on our paper and please find our answers to your questions below.

**Q1**:"Different groups in LSC for CIFAR-10 are manually created. How to...."

**A1**:The LSC value is a hyperparameter in our algorithm, and it is not sensitive to different new models. It is sensitive to the classes of the dataset, such as CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. We can estimate the LSC value according to the number of categories of the dataset. For example, 1.5 can achieve good results for both CIFAR-10 and SVHN, and 4 for CIFAR-100. Thanks for your valuable comments, we will clarify this in the revision.

**Q2**:"Improvement of results for CIFAR-100 are marginal over the baseline. Does it...."

**A2**:It is very time-consuming to draw weight loss landscapes across attack modes, networks and datasets. Instead, we verify the phenomenon (the model first overfits some easy-to-learn examples, and then expands to the entire dataset) by removing the training examples. Specifically, during the adversarial training process, we remove training examples whose loss value is lower than the LSC value. In this way, we demonstrate the generalities of the phenomenon under different attack modes, different datasets and different networks, as shown in the Appendix of revision. We observed that this phenomenon is not evident in the CIFAR-100 dataset. We believe that the main reasons are 1)classification task in CIFAR100 dataset is challenging, and the proportion of easy-to-learn examples in the dataset is small; 2)the number of training examples per class are small, and the removal of training examples can easily lead to problems such as example imbalance. Since this phenomenon is not evident in CIFAR100, we need a larger LSC value in our algorithm to eliminate robust overfitting, which also leads to the performance improvement of our algorithm over AWP in CIFAR100 is not significant. Nonetheless, stable performance improvements on CIFAR100 can be achieved. Thanks for your valuable comments, we will clarify this in the revision.

**Q3**:"The improvements of TRADES-AWP and RST-AWP on CIFAR-10 are also marginal. This reveals...."

**A3**:As mentioned in **A2**, this phenomenon is significant in CIFAR10 and SVHN. In our experiments, the performance improvement is also very obvious. It is worth noting that in the submitted paper, we directly quoted the experimental results of the original paper AWP, which is somewhat different from the performance we achieved. In our experiments, the results of Table 2 are as follows:

|  Defense   | Natural  | FGSM  |  PGD-20  |  PGD-100  |  C&W  |  AA  | 
|  ----  | ----  | ----  | ----  | ----  | ----  | ----  |
| AT  | 86.52 | 61.91 | 55.47 | 55.15 | 54.51 | 52.18 |
| AT-AWP  | 85.67 | 64.31 | 58.57 | 58.46 | 55.78 | 53.63 |
| AT-RWP  | **86.86** | **66.22** | **62.87** | **62.87** | **56.62** | **54.61** |
| TRADES  | 84.42 | 61.20 | 56.05 | 55.85 | 53.67 | 52.64 |
| TRADES-AWP  | 84.55 | 62.99 | 59.2 | 59.05 | 55.92 | 55.32 |
| TRADES-RWP  | **86.14** | **64.70** | **60.45** | **60.30** | **58.07** | **57.20** |
| RST  | **89.88** | **70.08** | 62.4 | 62.08 | 61.14 | 59.71 |
| RST-AWP  | 88.01 | 68 | 63.67 | 63.5 | 60.55 | 59.8 |
| RST-RWP  | 88.87 | 69.71 | **64.11** | **63.92** | **62.03** | **60.36** |

All codes of AWP and RWP are provided in the supplementary material. The AWP algorithm comes from [AWP](https://github.com/csdongxian/AWP). The above results can be verified by the code in the supplementary material. Actually, our performance improvement is more significant than that shown on the submitted paper.

**Q4**:"Given the statement "Without an appropriate criterion to regulate...... unleash its full power" in
the Introduction...."

**A4**:If there is no robust overfitting in adversarial training, then the standard adversarial training without weight perturbation should be able to achieve better adversarial robustness. Adversarial weight perturbation can suppress robust overfitting, which brings a certain degree of robustness improvement, but weight perturbation itself hinders network optimization to some extent. Thank you very much for your kind suggestions. We will clarify this in the revision.

We will revise our paper based on your valuable reviews. Please let us know if you have any further comments. We will try our best to address them and improve our paper.
